content: HIBERIX is a sterile, freeze-dried powder that must be reconstituted with the provided saline diluent before administration via intramuscular injection. The vaccine contains the capsular polysaccharide of Haemophilus influenzae type b (polyribosyl-ribitol-phosphate), which is a high molecular weight polymer derived from the Haemophilus influenzae type b strain 20,752. This strain is cultivated in a synthetic medium, then subjected to heat inactivation and purification processes. The vaccine also includes tetanus toxoid, which is produced from Clostridium tetani grown in a semi-synthetic medium. The tetanus toxin is detoxified using formaldehyde and subsequently purified. The capsular polysaccharide is chemically conjugated to the tetanus toxoid. After undergoing purification, the conjugate is freeze-dried in the presence of lactose, which serves as a stabilizing agent. The diluent provided for reconstitution is a sterile saline solution containing 0.9% sodium chloride, supplied in prefilled TIP-LOK syringes. Once reconstituted, each dose of HIBERIX contains 10 micrograms of purified capsular polysaccharide conjugated to approximately 25 micrograms of tetanus toxoid, 12.6 milligrams of lactose, and no more than 0.5 micrograms of residual formaldehyde. The vaccine does not include any preservatives. It is important to note that the tip caps of the prefilled syringes may contain natural rubber latex. However, the rubber plungers of the syringes and the stoppers of the vials are latex-free.
